title: Sir Geoffrey Wilkinson Lecture 2026 – Towards Solar Fuels and Fertilisers
desc:
Towards Solar Fuels and Fertilisers: Managing Proton and Electron Currency through Molecular Design

Life runs on electrons and protons. Together, or as hydrogen-atom equivalents, they allow plants to store solar energy, underpin the fuels that power society, and help make the fertilisers needed to sustain life.

Simply put, hydrogen atoms decorate many of the key molecular building blocks of our world. Chemists would like to harness this same basic currency to make fuels, fertilisers, and other useful molecules using renewable electricity or light.

The challenge is control. Protons and electrons readily combine to make hydrogen gas, often more easily than they can be directed toward other molecules. Learning how to steer them selectively is therefore a central problem in modern…

title: Structures Seminar: Towards Reliable Self-Generating Digital Twins through AI-Enabled Reconstruction of Missing Structural Monitoring Data
desc:
Abstract:

Digital Twins integrate computational models with monitoring data to represent structural behaviour and support the assessment of civil infrastructure. Achieving sustained synchronisation between physical structures and their digital counterparts requires these systems to adapt to changing structural conditions and evolving data availability. A Self-Generating Digital Twin (SGDT) is conceived as a full realisation of a true Digital Twin: one that continuously updates, learns and evolves through autonomous data assimilation and model regeneration. Within this framework, incomplete monitoring data present a critical challenge, potentially compromising the information required for reliable structural-response estimation and model updating. This seminar presents research…

title: Control and Optimisation seminar – Eugene Feinberg (Stony Brook University)
desc:
Title

Dynamically Augmented CVaR for Markov Decision Processes

Abstract

This talk describes a new approach to optimization of Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) for Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) with finite state and action sets. It introduces the Dynamically augmented CVaR (DCVaR) risk objective function and provides an algorithm for its optimization. CVaR optimization for MDPs is relevant to a specially defined Robust MDP (RMDP), in which the state space is augmented with the tail risk level. This RMDP, which we call the Dynamically augmented RMDP (DRMDP), was introduced to the literature for calculations of optimal CVaR values by value iteration more than ten years ago, but, as was understood later, these value iterations compute lower bounds of minimal static CVaRs. title: HEP seminar: Michael Revering (Cambridge) – Extending the LHC reach to very long lifetimes: the design concept and current status of the ANUBIS experiment
desc: Many beyond-the-standard model theories propose the existence of new ‘long-lived’ particles (LLPs) with macroscopic decay lengths that may be produced in high energy collisions at the LHC. While extensive searches for LLPs have been performed by existing LHC experiments such as ATLAS, CMS, and LHCb, their sensitivity to very long-lived models (ct>~10 m) is constrained by the physical size of the detectors. The proposed ANUBIS experiment is designed to significantly extend experimental sensitivity to these very long-lived models by instrumenting the ceiling of the ATLAS detector cavern with RPC detectors. In addition to extending the decay volume, the transverse positioning provides sensitivity to LLP models with high-mass mediators, complementing the sensitivity of existing forward…

title: SPC Seminar – Climate – Tom Goren (BIU)
desc:
Speaker: Tom Goren (BIU)

Title: A Ternary Framework for Marine Stratocumulus Morphology and Aerosol-Cloud Interactions

Abstract: Marine low-level clouds span a continuum of morphologies but are often classified into discrete regimes. I will present a new ternary framework that captures this continuum and provides insights into cloud morphological evolution and the underlying physical processes. The framework also allows us to better characterize how cloud responses to changes in droplet number concentration depend on morphology. The results reveal considerable variability in the contributions of liquid water path, cloud cover, and the Twomey effect to the overall cloud albedo response, with these contributions either offsetting or amplifying one another. title: Analysis and Dynamics seminar: Raz Slutsky (University of Oxford)
desc:
Speaker: Raz Slutsky (Oxford) Title: Random sparsification, torsion in homology, and fixed price

Abstract: Given a complicated geometric object, we often want to simplify it without losing information about the structure we are interested in. In this talk, I will describe a method for doing this by combining a random sparse set with a deterministic one, gaining some of the advantages of both. We will then see how this idea can be used to show that torsion in the first homology of higher-rank lattices grows subexponentially, answering a question of Abért, Gelander, and Nikolov and confirming the degree-one case of several conjectures. We will also use the same principle to give a new general criterion for a dynamical property known as fixed price one, which applies to a broad class of…
